meta.expect: answers in first person, no narration, no invented evidence

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until twenty to five, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first: who decided that, and on what basis?
You asked for this meeting, Hale, so skip the pleasantries. Who entered that zero, and did anyone hear Owen first?
Seventeen, and he lives at home with me. That makes me the parent your own procedure 4.2 says you contact before any mark goes in, and nobody did.

What does his job have to do with his essay, Hale? Twelve minutes left before I'm in the principal's office instead of here.



Wait—clock: started 4:15, she has to 4:40; it's not that late yet. Don't invent "twelve minutes". Let me rewrite properly.

What does his job have to do with his essay, Hale? You're fishing, and I don't have time for it.
When did his dad move out?
That's not yours to ask, and I'm not answering it. If you have something about Owen's essay, put it on the table now.
And what day was the zero entered?
Tuesday, November 3, and he handed the essay in on Thursday, October 29. You entered it, so you tell me who you spoke to between those two dates.
What do you know about his essay so far?
I know he wrote it over the weekend, and I know a piece of software flagged it. Is that all you have, or is there something else?
